marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q001.explanation: In the human body, water constitutes the highest proportion of body weight. The total body water accounts for ~60% of body weight.

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q002.explanation:
When expressed as the percentage of body weight, 40% of body weight is in ICF (2/3rd of 60%), and 20% of body weight is in ECF (1/3rd of 60%).

The 60-40-20 rule is: 60% of body weight is water, 40% is ICF, and 20% is ECF.

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q003.explanation:
His total blood volume is 5 litres.

Calculation:

Total blood volume = Plasma volume / (1 - Hematocrit)
Total blood volume = 3 L / (1 - 0.4) = 5 L

Hematocrit is a percentage, as it is 40% which equals 40/100 = 0.4.

(Normally, total blood volume is 8% of body weight).

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q004.explanation:
The total blood volume of a child is around 75–80 mL/kg.
In the neonatal period, it is 85 mL/kg. It rises to a peak of 105 mL/kg by the end of the first month and then drops progressively over ensuing months.

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q005.explanation:
The water content of lean body tissue is constant at 71–72 mL/100 g of tissue.

Lean body mass = Body mass - (Adipose tissue fat mass + Bone Mass + Non-Adipose Tissue Fat Mass)

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q006.explanation:
The volume of a fluid compartment in the body can be measured by "indicator (dye)-dilution" method. This method is based on the conservation of mass principle, which means that the total mass of a substance after dispersion in the fluid compartment will be the same as the total mass injected into the compartment.

If none of the substance leaks out of the compartment, the total mass of substance in the compartment (Volume B × Concentration B) will equal the total mass of the substance injected (Volume A × Concentration A). By simple rearrangement of the equation, one can calculate the unknown volume of chamber B:

Volume B = (Volume A × Concentration A) / Concentration B

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q007.explanation:
The volume of distribution can be calculated using the formula:

V = (Amount injected - Amount excreted) / Concentration

• V = volume of compartment
• Amount injected = 500 mg
• Amount of indicator excreted = 10% of 500 mg = 50 mg
• Plasma concentration of the indicator = 3.2 mg/100 mL

Calculation:
V = (500 mg - 50 mg) / (3.2 mg/100 mL) = 14.1 L

2nd method:
Mannitol is a substance which leaves blood vessel but can't enter the cell. Therefore, after attaining equilibrium, concentration of mannitol is same in plasma and interstitial fluid. Therefore, by applying dye-dilution technique, mannitol can be used to measure the volume of ECF (x).

Since, 10% is excreted and 10% of 500 mg is 50 mg, the amount of mannitol diluted in ECF is 450 mg (500 - 50), i.e. 450 mg is present in x. From the given values, 3.2 mg is present in 100 mL, which can be re-written as 3.2/100 = 450/x. Therefore x = 450 × 100 / 3.2 mL = 14,062.5 mL = 14 L.

Clinical:
IV Mannitol is used to treat cerebral oedema (since, it doesn't cross cell membrane it extracts fluid from brain cells), whereas it is contraindicated in pulmonary edema (here the fluid collection is in the interstitial space).

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q008.explanation:
Inulin is the indicator used to measure the ECF volume. (Since, inulin can cross blood vessel but not cell wall.)

Calculation:
• Since 10% is excreted, volume of inulin excreted is 1 gm. The amount of inulin diluted in ECF is 9 g (10 - 1), i.e. 9 g is present in x.
• From the given values, 50 mg is present in 100 mL, which can be re-written as 50/100 = 9000/x.
• x = 9000 × 100 / 50 = 18,000 mL = 18 L.

Second method:
• Since 10% is excreted, volume of inulin excreted is 1 gm.
• Amount injected = 10 g.
• Amount excreted = 1 g.
• Now, the concentration of inulin after equilibrium is 50 mg/100 mL which is equal to 0.05 g/100 mL.
Therefore, fluid volume = (10 - 1) × 100 / 0.05 = 18,000 mL = 18 L.

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q009.explanation:
The ECF volume can be estimated using any of several substances that disperse in the plasma and interstitial fluid but do not readily penetrate the cell membrane.

Example - radioactive sodium, thiosulfate ion and inulin.

Hint: Sodium (Na+) can cross blood vessel but not cell wall passively (therefore used to measure ECF volume).

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q010.explanation:
As the dye diffuses out of the capillaries, the measured concentration of the dye after equilibrium will be less. So, as per the formula, the volume measured will be falsely high.

V = (Amount Injected - Amount Excreted) / Plasma concentration of dye

Detailed explanation:
• Dye X measures plasma volume: dye X doesn't have the property of crossing blood vessel. If the dye X has been used properly, for a normal person then the value would come around 3 L.
• Dye Y crosses capillaries, which means it can cross any blood vessel. This property is used to measure the value of ECF. If the dye Y is given, for a normal person then the value would come around 14 L.
• Thus if dye Y is given in place of X, then the value would be 14 instead of 3 which is a false and the obtained value is high when compared to normal value.
• Therefore the answer is falsely high.

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q011.explanation:
Interstitial fluid volume is best measured using a combination of inulin and Evans blue.
Interstitial fluid is measured indirectly. ECF minus plasma volume gives the interstitial fluid value.

• Best measure of ECF - Inulin
• Best measure of Plasma Volume - Evans Blue (T1824)

marrow__PHYS_CH05_Q012.explanation: The pH of ECF is 7.4 while the pH of ICF is 7.0. There is continuous generation of H+ ions in the ICF due to the various metabolic processes. So, the pH of ICF is little lower compared to ECF.
